english.title: Falsely hold self out as registered trade mark agent or attorney
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in the course of a business,

(A)_[described or held yourself out]_
(B)_[permitted yourself to be described or held out]_

as a registered trade mark

(C)_[agent]_
(D)_[attorney]_

when not a registered trade mark attorney
english.legislation: Contrary to section 84(1)(b) and (4) of the Trade Marks Act 1994.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
in the course of a business
described/held yourself out/permitted yourself to be described/held out
as a registered trade mark agent/attorney
when not a registered trade mark attorney

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes: Regarding the time limit for prosecutions, see section 84(4).
english.standardstatementoffacts:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, in the course of a business,

(A)_[described or held himself out]_
(B)_[described or held herself out]_
(C)_[permitted himself to be described or held out]_
(D)_[permitted herself to be described or held out]_

as a registered trade mark

(E)_[agent]_
(F)_[attorney]_

when not a registered trade mark attorney.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 84(4)

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
